question_text: Who is responsible for the roadworthiness of a licensed vehicle?
comment: Responsible for the roadworthy condition of a vehicle are both the owner of the vehicle as well as the driver. The driver has to check the operational reliability as well as roadworthiness of the vehicle before driving. The owner has to make sure that this actually happens. This also applies to the TÜV examination. The liability insurance is not responsible.

question_text: What must you do when you are travelling and you notice that your vehicle is no longer roadworthy?

options.text: Take the vehicle out of the traffic as quickly as possible
Continue only when the damage has been repaired
Proceed to the next authorised dealer

correct_answers.text: Take the vehicle out of the traffic as quickly as possible
Continue only when the damage has been repaired

comment: If a vehicle is not roadworthy, the driver must remove it from traffic as soon as possible. Note that driving to the nearest workshop is also prohibited. Only after the damage has been repaired, you may continue driving.

question_text: Which defects of a vehicle can result in a danger for road traffic?
comment: Worn tires have a negative effect on the grip and could lead the car to skidding. Defective tail lamps make the car less visible to the surrounding traffic. Insufficient braking action can lead to a prolonged braking distance therefore lead to higher risk of accidents, especially for rear-end collisions. All three defects lead to a threat to traffic safety.

question_text: You want to make a telephone call while driving a vehicle. What must you be aware of?

options.text: I may be distracted by the call
I may be distracted through operating the telephone
Telephoning using a hands-free unit does not distract me

correct_answers.text: I may be distracted by the call
I may be distracted through operating the telephone

comment: Being on the phone or operating a telephone while driving distracts the driver. Even if you're using a hands-free kit, you'll need to keep in mind that some of your senses are distracted and you cannot focus entirely on driving.

question_text: You want to make a telephone call while driving. What must you be aware of?

options.text: I need to have a hands-free unit
I may use the telephone without a hands-free unit, if the vehicle is parked in a suitable place, and the engine is fully switched off
I may use the telephone without a hands-free, if the vehicle is moving at walking pace

correct_answers.text: I need to have a hands-free unit
I may use the telephone without a hands-free unit, if the vehicle is parked in a suitable place, and the engine is fully switched off

comment: While driving, you're only allowed to use the speaker phone. If you do not have a hands-free kit, you must drive to a suitable location and stop the engine completely. Only then you are allowed to use your mobile phone. To use your phone while driving without hands-free equipment is a serious offense, a so-called A-offense, with high penalties.

question_text: You want to use a motor vehicle on public roads. What must you observe?

options.text: The motor vehicle must be roadworthy
The motor vehicle must be covered by liability insurance
I must be the vehicle owner

correct_answers.text: The motor vehicle must be roadworthy
The motor vehicle must be covered by liability insurance

comment: You may only use a vehicle on public roads if it is roadworthy and if there is liability insurance for the vehicle.
